tasks.short: Confer with therapy staff on the patient's treatment.

steps.what: Read the posted treatment line for this patient.
Confer with therapy staff on this patient's treatment.

tasks.design: The therapy assistant still confers with therapy staff on this patient's treatment. A treatment line is already posted in the {DOCS}, with patient code, topic, date, focus and the author's name, so the hunt for that sheet is shorter. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: The treatment line sat on a paper sheet, so the assistant hunted it before conferring with the staff.
tasks.enabler_now: The patient file already holds a treatment line. Showing patient code, topic, date, focus and the author's name is configuration of that file.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the staff conference changes the treatment is what happens in the room. A posted line does not confer.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant hears the staff and the patient and refuses a line that does not name this patient.
tasks.altitude: The week is still the treatment room. Less time goes to hunting a treatment sheet. The assistant still confers.

reach.task: Post the treatment line before the conference.
reach.learn: The line needs patient code, topic, date, focus and the author's name, or the assistant reads the paper sheet.

reach.task: Leave the conference with the assistant.
reach.learn: Conferring with therapy staff is a talk inside the organisation. It is not a send.

reach.task: Stay out of the conference unless asked.
reach.learn: The assistant still confers. The aide does not replace the staff talk.

evidence.claim: Conferring with therapy staff on a patient's treatment stays with the therapy assistant. A posted treatment line can be a shorter read. The conference itself is not shorter. Model knowledge.
The therapist keeps a dossier with the health data needed for good care, for 20 years. This design does not enter the conference into that dossier.
Physiotherapists are registered for individual health care. Assistants and aides are not. This design does not let the assistant set the treatment plan or a diagnosis.
Recordings and notes are health data. This design makes no recording of the conference and adds no note.
A tool that proposes a diagnosis or a treatment is a higher-class device. This design proposes neither, and it makes no transcript.
At a larger practice or a rehabilitation centre, recording staff conversations needs works-council consent. This design does not record the conference and does not monitor the assistant.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: this task is only conferring with therapy staff about this patient's treatment. Measuring, instructing family, training on a device, billing, scheduling, supplies and progress notes sit outside it. The physical therapist posts the line before the conference.

Structured input: one treatment line in the {DOCS} with patient code, topic, date, focus and the author's name. The line is the plan focus, not a progress note and not a measured value. If the line is missing or free text, the assistant reads the paper sheet and that read is not shorter.

The assistant still confers in the room. Nothing is recorded by a machine, sent, or committed. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. There is no commit and no send, so there is no gate on a sent version. The prior that conferring is a send outside the organisation is refused: it is a talk with colleagues, and it is a write inside the organisation. The prior that a person must approve a sent version is refused: nothing is sent or committed.

A model is not used. The prior that a model is needed is refused: the assistant has to confer. The prior that this is a dashboard is refused. Existing system runtime is not the assistant's time. The design does not diagnose, propose a treatment, record the conference, monitor the assistant, or file a note.
unknowns: Whether this patient file already has patient code, topic, date, focus and a name, or only a paper sheet.
Whether the practice later wants the conference filed in the dossier. This design does not file it.
research_questions: Who posts the treatment line, the physical therapist or a colleague?
What share of conferences start with no line the assistant can read?

already_counted.description: Reading a missing or free-text treatment sheet by hand, inside the remaining read.

incremental.description: Checking that the treatment line still names this patient, topic, date, focus and an author.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the treatment line is often missing or free text, so the assistant still hunts the paper sheet and the read is not shorter. High: most lines carry patient code, topic, date, focus and an author's name, and only that hunt shrinks. Conferring stays. The high stays under the net after the field check.
